summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32 and Raspberry Pi platforms. Built bare-metal embedded C firmware with low-level device drivers (GPIO, ADC, I2C, UART) and RTOS task/mutex coordination on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers. Comfortable troubleshooting hardware/software integration end-to-end, using Git for version control across every build.

Embedded & Firmware: Low-level device drivers (GPIO, ADC, I2C, UART, PWM)

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via embedded Python firmware.
Resolved sensor jitter through hardware debugging of a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding, software calibration, and ADC resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team end-to-end across national competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and hardware/software integration.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented low-level device drivers for sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a Python GUI (PyQt/Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory hardware environment.
Used Git-based version control (GitLab) and JupyterHub for collaborative technical documentation across a multi-engineer research team.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal embedded C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on an ARM Cortex-M4, achieving 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C device driver for real-time embedded sensing.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on an ARM Cortex-M microcontroller, integrating VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override on STM32 embedded firmware.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
